title: Musk escalates Ambani feud, shares reports alleging Reliance links to BJP campaign boosts, donations
key_facts: On Saturday 10 Oct 2026 Musk posted on X screenshots of a 2022 Al Jazeera report that a Reliance-funded firm boosted BJP campaigns on Facebook and a 2024 Indian Express report that a Reliance-linked firm (Qwik Supply) donated Rs 385 crore to the BJP via electoral bonds.
Hours earlier Musk addressed Mukesh Ambani as 'Prime Minister Ambani' and accused him of protecting a monopoly.
The feud stems from the delay in launching Starlink satellite broadband in India.
The government says its authorisation framework for telecom and satellite services is 'fair and non-discriminatory' and any suggestion it is applied selectively is 'baseless and misconceived'.

On 9 Oct Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said three firms hold satcom licences (Starlink, Jio Satcom, Eutelsat OneWeb) and can start after meeting security conditions and once spectrum charges are set.
TRAI and the telecom department are close to a final decision on satcom spectrum pricing, Scindia said.
quote_evidence: Reliance has not publicly responded to Musk's allegations, while the government has maintained that the country's authorisation framework for telecom and satellite services is "fair and non-discriminatory".
Scindia said three entities - Musk's Starlink, Reliance Jio's satellite venture Jio Satcom, Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb - have already secured licences.
Starlink is licensed in over 165 countries and has spent five years complying with every single law and requirement of the government of India, so why still no license?
why_it_matters_hint: Decides nothing yet but bears on when people in India can buy Starlink; the Reliance allegations are Musk's, shared from older reports.
notes: Continues the BBC item of our 9 Oct 2026 edition. The reports Musk shared are from 2022 and 2024; the article does not say they were verified today.
